subject: SELF and SUPER
notes: kb/Work PB1425 (w1021a). "SUPER may be specified only as the object in an object-property identifier or as the object used to invoke a method with the INVOKE statement or an inline invocation of a method" (cite.py --check 8.4.3.8.3 -> OK 3)). All three homes are legal: INVOKE SUPER / [K OF] SUPER ::, and now the object of a property - BAL OF SUPER and BAL OF K OF SUPER read and write through the base class's accessor (base.<accessor>, 8.4.3.8.4 GR3 / GR4: the golden's PB1425FB overrides GET PROPERTY BAL, and BAL OF SUPER still answers its base's 100). Every other position refuses it by this rule, COBOL2900: a bare SUPER operand (OoBindSelfOperand) and the qualified `K OF SUPER` operand, which the grammar spells as the chain `K OF SUPER` and the resolver tells from the property K of SUPER by the declared name (QualifiedSuperClass). [editions: the OO facility, 2002+] retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/ReferenceResolver.cs#OoTryBindPropertyReference (the one-word property binder ReferenceResolver.OoTryBindPropertyReference is deleted by kb/Work PB1425 (w1021a): a property reference is resolved by ReferenceResolver.ResolveObjectProperty, which splits the chain and resolves identifier-3 through the ordinary resolver)
